    for y in range(h):

# group adjacent columns into runs (stripes) with tolerance

        # drift the reference slightly
        cur = tuple((cur[i]*3+cols[x][i])//4 for i in range(3))

"**Hello**" is a song recorded by British singer-songwriter [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele"), released on 23 October 2015 by [XL Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XL_Recordings "XL Recordings") as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from her third studio album, *[25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25_\(Adele_album\) "25 (Adele album)")* (2015). Written by Adele and the album's producer, [Greg Kurstin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kurstin "Greg Kurstin"), "Hello" is a [piano ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_ballade "Piano ballade") with [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") influences (including guitar) and lyrics that discuss themes of nostalgia and regret. Upon release, the song garnered critical acclaim, with reviewers comparing it favourably to Adele's previous works and praised its lyrics, production and Adele's vocal performance. It was recorded in [Metropolis Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_Group "Metropolis Group"), London.

"Hello" was a massive global success. The single charted in a record-setting 30 countries, including in the United Kingdom where it became Adele's second chart topper, following "[Someone Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\) "Someone like You (Adele song)")"; it also had the largest opening week sales in three years. In the United States, "Hello" debuted atop the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), reigning for ten consecutive weeks while becoming Adele's fourth number-one single on the chart and breaking several records, including becoming the first song to sell over a million digital copies in a week. By the end of 2015, it had sold 12\.3 million units globally (combined sales and track-equivalent streams) and was the year's 7th best-selling single while it stands as one of the [best-selling digital singles of all-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_digital_singles "List of best-selling singles").[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

The accompanying music video was directed by [Xavier Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Dolan "Xavier Dolan") and co-stars Adele and [Tristan Wilds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tristan_Wilds "Tristan Wilds"). It broke the [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") and YouTube records for achieving over 27\.7 million views within a 24-hour span, and the record for the shortest time to reach one billion views (87 days) respectively.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Guiness-4) "Hello" broke the [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") records for being number 1 in most countries (102 countries).[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The music video for the song received seven nominations at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards"), including [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") and [Best Female Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Female_Video "MTV Video Music Award for Best Female Video").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) At the [59th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards"), "Hello" won three awards: [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), and [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The song also won the [Brit Award for British Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single"),[\[8\]](#cite_note-McGeorge_2016-8) and [APRA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APRA_Awards_\(Australia\) "APRA Awards (Australia)") for International Work of the Year.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

"Hello" was written by Adele and [Greg Kurstin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kurstin "Greg Kurstin") and produced by Kurstin, who also played bass, guitar, drums, piano and keyboards, while Adele played drums.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) "Hello" was written in [Chiswick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiswick "Chiswick"), London, something not normally done by Adele, who said she likes to write her music at home.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) The writing process for the song was slow, taking six months to complete. Initially Adele and Kurstin started writing the first verse; finishing half of the song, six months later Adele contacted Kurstin to finish the song with her, with Kurstin stating he was not sure "if Adele was ever going to come back and finish it."[\[13\]](#cite_note-RTm-13)

"Hello" is a [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") piano ballad,[\[2\]](#cite_note-SGum-2)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) played in the key of [F minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_minor "F minor") at a tempo of 79 beats per minute. The repeated chord progression heard in the verse, played by the piano, follows two progressions and a passage (Bridge) progression (passage or Bridge progression connects two main progressions to each other) of Progression \#1: Fm(i)–A♭(III)–E♭(VII)–D♭(VI), Passage progression: Fm(i)–E♭(VII)-Cm(v)-D♭(VI)-Fm7(i7)-E♭(VII)–D♭(VI), Progression \#2:Fm(i)–D♭/F(VI)–A♭(III)–E♭(VII). According to Musicnotes.com, Adele's vocals span from F3 to A♭5 in the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Vocalrange-15) During the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain"), Adele is heard singing the lines over layers of backing vocals, piano and drums which were described by *[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* as having "a very luscious wall of sound".[\[10\]](#cite_note-telegraph-10)

Lyrically, the song focuses on themes of nostalgia and regret, and was seen as a follow-up to her single "Someone like You" appearing to reflect on a failed relationship. The song's lyrics were also seen as being conversational, revolving around "all the relationships of her past", ranging from friends, family members and ex-partners.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) Speaking on the song's lyrical content, Adele told [Nick Grimshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Grimshaw "Nick Grimshaw") on *[The Radio 1 Breakfast Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_1_Breakfast "Radio 1 Breakfast")*: "I felt all of us were moving on, and it's not about an ex-relationship, a love relationship, it's about my relationship with everyone that I love. It's not that we have fallen out, we've all got our lives going on and I needed to write that song so they would all hear it, because I'm not in touch with them."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) According to Adele, the line "Hello from the other side" signifies "the other side of becoming an adult, making it out alive from your late teens, early twenties."[\[13\]](#cite_note-RTm-13)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")\]

On 18 October 2015, a 30-second clip of "Hello" was played during a commercial break on *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* in the United Kingdom. The commercial teased what was then new material, with her vocals accompanied by lyrics on a black screen.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Josh Duboff of *[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_\(magazine\) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")* wrote that "the Internet collectively lost their minds" after the broadcast of the trailer.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) On 22 October, Adele announced the upcoming release of *25* to her fans on Twitter. She also shared that "Hello" would be released on 23 October as the lead single off of the album.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](#cite_note-CoS-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-AXS-22) On 23 October, Adele joined [Nick Grimshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Grimshaw "Nick Grimshaw")'s show on [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1") for the song's premiere.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Hello" received universal critical acclaim.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* described it as "a big ballad, but a superior example of its kind", and opined that the song is "precisely the kind of lovelorn epic ballad that made Adele one of the biggest stars in the world."[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Writing for *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")*, Emily Jupp stated in her review of the song that it "might not be groundbreaking, but Adele's return with her familiar, smoky sound is very welcome". She called it an "'if it ain't broke' ballad" and said: "Adele does what she does best, belting out emotional tales of love and loss much the same as with her last album, *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")*, but this time, with a little more self-forgiveness."[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

[Greg Kot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kot "Greg Kot") of the *[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")* wrote: "Lyrics that work best when they zoom in on personal details match her combination of vocal power and restraint."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Neil McCormick from *[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* called it "a beautiful song of loss and regret", adding that "it takes a grip on the kind of memory every listener holds somewhere in their heart and merges it with Adele's own drama."[\[10\]](#cite_note-telegraph-10) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* ranked "Hello" at number 6 on its year-end list to find the 50 best songs of 2015\.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) Several publications have commented on similarities in the theme of the song and accompanying video with that of "[Hello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello_\(Lionel_Richie_song\) "Hello (Lionel Richie song)")" by American singer [Lionel Richie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Richie "Lionel Richie").[\[33\]](#cite_note-Horton-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

In 2021, *[Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parade_\(magazine\) "Parade (magazine)")* ranked the song number 12 on their list of the 25 greatest Adele songs.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Further, in 2022, *[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")* ranked the song number three on their list of the 10 greatest Adele songs.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

## Chart performance

### Europe and Oceania

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Europe and Oceania")\]

Three days after its release, the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company") announced that "Hello" had accumulated 165,000 chart sales in the United Kingdom, of which 156,000 were downloads.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) "Hello" entered at the top of the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on 30 October 2015, – for the week dated 5 November 2015 – with 333,000 combined sales, of which 259,000 were downloads, making it the biggest selling number-one single on the chart in three years. It marked Adele's second UK number-one single, after 2011's "Someone like You". Additionally, "Hello" was streamed 7\.32 million times in its first week, breaking the streaming record previously held by [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[What Do You Mean?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Do_You_Mean%3F "What Do You Mean?")". Including streaming sales and excluding *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* and *[Pop Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Idol "Pop Idol")* winners' singles, major charity campaign records and Christmas number ones, "Hello" was the second biggest selling number one of the 21st century in the UK, beaten only by [Shaggy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaggy_\(musician\) "Shaggy (musician)")'s "[It Wasn't Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Wasn't_Me "It Wasn't Me")", which sold 345,000 copies in a week in February 2001\.[\[38\]](#cite_note-UK_number_1-38) The following week, the song remained at number one after selling a further 121,000 downloads and was streamed 5\.78 million times, the same week the song was certified Gold by the BPI.[\[39\]](#cite_note-auto-39) On 20 May 2016, it spent its 30th week in the UK Top 100\. As of November 2016, the song has sold 918,700 in pure sales.[\[40\]](#cite_note-UK_sales-40)

The song also debuted at number one in Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Lebanon, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Scotland, Slovakia, Spain and Switzerland.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Idolator-41)

In Australia, "Hello" entered at the top of the [ARIA Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") on 31 October 2015, selling over 59,075 units, which earned the song a gold certification in its first week. The song also became the second fastest-selling single of the year, behind [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa")'s "[See You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/See_You_Again "See You Again")".[\[42\]](#cite_note-maricrisfaderugao-42) It marked Adele's second number-one single on the ARIA Singles Chart following 2011's "Someone like You".[\[43\]](#cite_note-AUS_number_1-43) The single stayed atop the chart for a second week and was certified platinum selling over 70,000 units.[\[42\]](#cite_note-maricrisfaderugao-42) On 20 March 2017, Hello re-entered the chart at number 50 and has so far been certified 7× platinum for sales over 490,000 units.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) In New Zealand, the song debuted at number one on the New Zealand singles chart, holding the position the following week and was certified platinum.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Idolator-41)

### North America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: North America")\]

In the United States, "Hello" debuted at the top of the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on 2 November 2015, for the chart dated 14 November 2015, becoming only the 24th song to debut at number one. "Hello" started at number 49 on the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, after three days of release. In its first full week of airplay, it rose from 45 to 9, up 146% to 70 million all format audience impressions. The track started at number one on the On-Demand Songs chart with a record 20\.4 million on-demand streams, becoming her first number-one song on the chart. "Hello" entered at the top of the [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart with sales of 1,112,000, becoming the first track to sell over one million digital copies in a single week and almost doubling the record for the most downloads sold in a week, previously held by [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida")'s "[Right Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_Round "Right Round")", which sold 636,000 downloads in the week ending 28 February 2009\. "Hello" started with 61\.6 million US streams, becoming her first number-one song and the second greatest weekly total on the [Streaming Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_Songs "Streaming Songs") chart, behind [Baauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baauer "Baauer")'s "[Harlem Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Shake_\(song\) "Harlem Shake (song)")", which registered 103 million streams on week of 3 March 2013\.[\[45\]](#cite_note-US_number_1-45) "Hello" is the first song to sell more than a million digital copies in a single week and the third highest weekly sales total since [Nielsen SoundScan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_SoundScan "Nielsen SoundScan") began tracking sales in 1991\. Only [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John")'s "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")/Something About the Way You Look Tonight" has sold more in a single week, selling 3\.446 million copies in its opening week and 1\.212 million copies in its second week.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

In its second week, "Hello" stayed at number one on the US *Billboard* Hot 100, selling another 635,000 digital copies marking the third-best digital sales week and the highest for a non-debut week. "Hello" also held atop Streaming Songs with 47\.4 million US streams, down 23 percent from 61\.6 million in its first week, the track also stayed atop the On-Demand Songs with 18\.1 million streams. On the Radio Songs chart, "Hello" moved from 9 to 6, up by 46% to 106 million all-format audience impressions, thus becoming the top Airplay Gainer on the Hot 100\. The track also moved from two to one on the Adult Alternative Songs airplay chart and moved nine to four on the Adult Contemporary format.[\[47\]](#cite_note-auto1-47) The following week, the song stayed at the top of the Hot 100 and Digital Songs chart, selling 480,000 downloads and becoming just the third song to sell over 400,000 copies for three straight weeks. "Hello" also rose from 6 to 1 on the Radio Songs chart in just its fourth week (the greatest leap to number one on the chart's 25-year history), marking the quickest climb to number one on the chart in 22 years, since [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")'s "[Dreamlover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamlover_\(Mariah_Carey_song\) "Dreamlover (Mariah Carey song)")" reached the top in its fourth frame on 28 August 1993\. Additionally, "Hello" became just the third song to top the [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100"), Digital Songs, Streaming Songs, On-Demand Songs and Radio Songs tallies simultaneously in the nearly three years all five charts had coexisted.[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) "Hello" remained atop the Hot 100 for ten consecutive weeks, becoming only the 31st No. 1 in the Hot 100's history to reign for at least 10 weeks, and only the 4th for a number one debut, following "[One Sweet Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Sweet_Day "One Sweet Day")" by Mariah Carey and [Boyz II Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyz_II_Men "Boyz II Men") (16 weeks), "Candle in the Wind 1997/Something About the Way You Look Tonight" by Elton John (14 weeks) and [I'll Be Missing You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Be_Missing_You "I'll Be Missing You") by [Puff Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Combs "Sean Combs") & [Faith Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Evans "Faith Evans") featuring [112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/112_\(band\) "112 (band)") (11 weeks). By spending a tenth week at the top of the chart, it became Adele's longest-running number-one single and the longest-leading Hot 100 No. 1 by a solo female since [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna")'s "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")," featuring [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris"), which also led for 10 weeks in 2011–2012. As of January 2016, it had sold 3\.7 million downloads.[\[49\]](#cite_note-ussales-49) The single also benefitted from numerous Dance/EDM remixes as well,[\[50\]](#cite_note-AdeleRemixes-50) thus resulting in "Hello" topping *Billboard's* [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") and [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") charts.[\[51\]](#cite_note-AdeleDanceCharts-51)[\[52\]](#cite_note-AdeleDanceNumberOne-52) On the chart dated 23 April 2016, the song spent a 21st week at the top of the [Adult Contemporary Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_Chart "Adult Contemporary Chart"), matching the record set by [Kelly Clarkson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Clarkson "Kelly Clarkson")'s "[Breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_\(Kelly_Clarkson_song\) "Breakaway (Kelly Clarkson song)")" (2005) and [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion")'s "[A New Day Has Come](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_New_Day_Has_Come_\(song\) "A New Day Has Come (song)")" (2002) for the longest No. 1 run among women since the list launched in 1961\. It also equaled the third-longest stay at the summit among all acts.[\[53\]](#cite_note-53) On 20 September 2016, the song was certified as seven-times platinum by [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[\[54\]](#cite_note-riaa-54)

"Hello" debuted at number one on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") on 3 November 2015, for the chart dated 14 November 2015, selling 140,000 copies and outsold [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[Sorry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorry_\(Justin_Bieber_song\) "Sorry (Justin Bieber song)")", which sold 40,000 units the same week. The song was streamed 4\.79 million times in its first week, setting a record for the most streamed track in a single week in Canada.[\[55\]](#cite_note-55)

Video of the Year") for "Hello".[\[58\]](#cite_note-58) Adele received four [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards") nominations, including Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber").[\[59\]](#cite_note-amas2016-59) At the [59th Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards") Adele took home five awards, including [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for *25*, while She also the first woman in Grammy history to win Song of the Year twice.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) This marks the first time in Grammy history that two different songs with the same title have been nominated in this category after "[Hello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello_\(Lionel_Richie_song\) "Hello (Lionel Richie song)")" by [Lionel Richie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Richie "Lionel Richie") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/27th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "27th Annual Grammy Awards").[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) Adele became the third woman to win Record of the Year more than once, after [Roberta Flack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_Flack "Roberta Flack") and [Norah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norah_Jones "Norah Jones") winning for *[The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_First_Time_Ever_I_Saw_Your_Face "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face")* and *[Killing Me Softly with His Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Me_Softly_with_His_Song "Killing Me Softly with His Song")*; and *[Don't Know Why](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Know_Why "Don't Know Why")* and *[Here We Go Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here_We_Go_Again_\(Ray_Charles_song\) "Here We Go Again (Ray Charles song)")* (with [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles")), respectively. ## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Music video")\]

> "When I heard the song I saw a story right away. \[The video\] is highly unoriginal. The lyrics are 'Hello, it's me' and then you see someone picking up a phone. I'm not good at imagining super conceptual videos. I just thought it would be nice to have her walk around the house and make phone calls and end up in a forest, with maybe some flashbacks in it."

— Xavier Dolan, behind the concept of the music video[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89)

The accompanying music video for "Hello" was directed by Canadian actor and filmmaker [Xavier Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Dolan "Xavier Dolan") and released on 23 October 2015, despite the fact the song was released as a single a day later.[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) The concept of the video revolves around a recently broken-up young woman calling a younger version of herself.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89) Portions of the video—mostly the finale on the pond and the shot of her opening her eyes in the beginning—were filmed with [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") cameras, making it the first music video in IMAX format.[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) The video draws inspiration from Dolan's semi-autobiographical debut *[I Killed My Mother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Killed_My_Mother "I Killed My Mother")*, which was made when Dolan was barely 20\.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89) The video was filmed on a farm in [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") over four days in September 2015\.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89)

The video stars American actor [Tristan Wilds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tristan_Wilds "Tristan Wilds"). According to Dolan, Adele called him after an unspecified incident of [police brutality in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_brutality_in_the_United_States "Police brutality in the United States"), suggesting that a white male not be cast as her love interest in the video. Dolan elaborated "She was just like, 'I'm concerned with the reality of the tensions between authorities and the black community, and I want to send a message out there.'"[\[93\]](#cite_note-93)[\[94\]](#cite_note-94) Dolan contacted Wilds via Skype and explained the concept for the video, which Wilds agreed to take part in.[\[95\]](#cite_note-ew.com-95) During the filming, both Adele and Wilds were asked to improvise and "tap into" their past relationships to convey the correct emotions. Dolan also filmed shots of both Adele and Wilds having conversations and laughing.[\[95\]](#cite_note-ew.com-95) The [sepia toned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepia_tone "Sepia tone") video shows Adele performing the song in a small house and outside in a wooded forest, intercut with scenes of her making a tearful phone call and flashbacks to a past relationship with Wilds' character.[\[96\]](#cite_note-96)

The [flip phone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_phone "Flip phone") used by Adele in the video was widely commented upon due to being of a [retro style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_style "Retro style"). Dolan replied to the remarks by saying: "It makes me uncomfortable filming iPhones because I feel like I'm shooting a commercial. Those things: iPhones, laptops, all those elements, to me, they bring me back to reality: That's not what you want. You want to get out of your own life; you want to enter someone else's; you want to travel somewhere; you want to be told a story. I'm realizing maybe I've been more distracting than anything else with that flip phone, but it wasn't intentional!"[\[97\]](#cite_note-97)

"**Hello**" is a song recorded by British singer-songwriter [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele"), released on 23 October 2015 by [XL Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XL_Recordings "XL Recordings") as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from her third studio album, *[25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25_\(Adele_album\) "25 (Adele album)")* (2015). Written by Adele and the album's producer, [Greg Kurstin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kurstin "Greg Kurstin"), "Hello" is a [piano ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_ballade "Piano ballade") with [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") influences (including guitar) and lyrics that discuss themes of nostalgia and regret. Upon release, the song garnered critical acclaim, with reviewers comparing it favourably to Adele's previous works and praised its lyrics, production and Adele's vocal performance. It was recorded in [Metropolis Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_Group "Metropolis Group"), London.

"Hello" was a massive global success. The single charted in a record-setting 30 countries, including in the United Kingdom where it became Adele's second chart topper, following "[Someone Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_like_You_\(Adele_song\) "Someone like You (Adele song)")"; it also had the largest opening week sales in three years. In the United States, "Hello" debuted atop the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), reigning for ten consecutive weeks while becoming Adele's fourth number-one single on the chart and breaking several records, including becoming the first song to sell over a million digital copies in a week. By the end of 2015, it had sold 12\.3 million units globally (combined sales and track-equivalent streams) and was the year's 7th best-selling single while it stands as one of the [best-selling digital singles of all-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_digital_singles "List of best-selling singles").[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

The accompanying music video was directed by [Xavier Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Dolan "Xavier Dolan") and co-stars Adele and [Tristan Wilds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tristan_Wilds "Tristan Wilds"). It broke the [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") and YouTube records for achieving over 27\.7 million views within a 24-hour span, and the record for the shortest time to reach one billion views (87 days) respectively.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Guiness-4) "Hello" broke the [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") records for being number 1 in most countries (102 countries).[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The music video for the song received seven nominations at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards"), including [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year") and [Best Female Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Female_Video "MTV Video Music Award for Best Female Video").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) At the [59th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards"), "Hello" won three awards: [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), and [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The song also won the [Brit Award for British Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single"),[\[8\]](#cite_note-McGeorge_2016-8) and [APRA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APRA_Awards_\(Australia\) "APRA Awards (Australia)") for International Work of the Year.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

## Writing and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Writing and composition")\]

![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

"Hello" was written by Adele and [Greg Kurstin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kurstin "Greg Kurstin") and produced by Kurstin, who also played bass, guitar, drums, piano and keyboards, while Adele played drums.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) "Hello" was written in [Chiswick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiswick "Chiswick"), London, something not normally done by Adele, who said she likes to write her music at home.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) The writing process for the song was slow, taking six months to complete. Initially Adele and Kurstin started writing the first verse; finishing half of the song, six months later Adele contacted Kurstin to finish the song with her, with Kurstin stating he was not sure "if Adele was ever going to come back and finish it."[\[13\]](#cite_note-RTm-13)

"Hello" is a [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") piano ballad,[\[2\]](#cite_note-SGum-2)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) played in the key of [F minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_minor "F minor") at a tempo of 79 beats per minute. The repeated chord progression heard in the verse, played by the piano, follows two progressions and a passage (Bridge) progression (passage or Bridge progression connects two main progressions to each other) of Progression \#1: Fm(i)–A♭(III)–E♭(VII)–D♭(VI), Passage progression: Fm(i)–E♭(VII)-Cm(v)-D♭(VI)-Fm7(i7)-E♭(VII)–D♭(VI), Progression \#2:Fm(i)–D♭/F(VI)–A♭(III)–E♭(VII). According to Musicnotes.com, Adele's vocals span from F3 to A♭5 in the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Vocalrange-15) During the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain"), Adele is heard singing the lines over layers of backing vocals, piano and drums which were described by *[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* as having "a very luscious wall of sound".[\[10\]](#cite_note-telegraph-10)

Lyrically, the song focuses on themes of nostalgia and regret, and was seen as a follow-up to her single "Someone like You" appearing to reflect on a failed relationship. The song's lyrics were also seen as being conversational, revolving around "all the relationships of her past", ranging from friends, family members and ex-partners.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) Speaking on the song's lyrical content, Adele told [Nick Grimshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Grimshaw "Nick Grimshaw") on *[The Radio 1 Breakfast Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_1_Breakfast "Radio 1 Breakfast")*: "I felt all of us were moving on, and it's not about an ex-relationship, a love relationship, it's about my relationship with everyone that I love. It's not that we have fallen out, we've all got our lives going on and I needed to write that song so they would all hear it, because I'm not in touch with them."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) According to Adele, the line "Hello from the other side" signifies "the other side of becoming an adult, making it out alive from your late teens, early twenties."[\[13\]](#cite_note-RTm-13)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")\]

On 18 October 2015, a 30-second clip of "Hello" was played during a commercial break on *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* in the United Kingdom. The commercial teased what was then new material, with her vocals accompanied by lyrics on a black screen.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Josh Duboff of *[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_\(magazine\) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")* wrote that "the Internet collectively lost their minds" after the broadcast of the trailer.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) On 22 October, Adele announced the upcoming release of *25* to her fans on Twitter. She also shared that "Hello" would be released on 23 October as the lead single off of the album.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](#cite_note-CoS-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-AXS-22) On 23 October, Adele joined [Nick Grimshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Grimshaw "Nick Grimshaw")'s show on [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1") for the song's premiere.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Hello" received universal critical acclaim.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* described it as "a big ballad, but a superior example of its kind", and opined that the song is "precisely the kind of lovelorn epic ballad that made Adele one of the biggest stars in the world."[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Writing for *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")*, Emily Jupp stated in her review of the song that it "might not be groundbreaking, but Adele's return with her familiar, smoky sound is very welcome". She called it an "'if it ain't broke' ballad" and said: "Adele does what she does best, belting out emotional tales of love and loss much the same as with her last album, *[21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_\(Adele_album\) "21 (Adele album)")*, but this time, with a little more self-forgiveness."[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

[Greg Kot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kot "Greg Kot") of the *[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")* wrote: "Lyrics that work best when they zoom in on personal details match her combination of vocal power and restraint."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Neil McCormick from *[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* called it "a beautiful song of loss and regret", adding that "it takes a grip on the kind of memory every listener holds somewhere in their heart and merges it with Adele's own drama."[\[10\]](#cite_note-telegraph-10) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* ranked "Hello" at number 6 on its year-end list to find the 50 best songs of 2015\.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) Several publications have commented on similarities in the theme of the song and accompanying video with that of "[Hello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello_\(Lionel_Richie_song\) "Hello (Lionel Richie song)")" by American singer [Lionel Richie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Richie "Lionel Richie").[\[33\]](#cite_note-Horton-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

In 2021, *[Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parade_\(magazine\) "Parade (magazine)")* ranked the song number 12 on their list of the 25 greatest Adele songs.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Further, in 2022, *[American Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Songwriter "American Songwriter")* ranked the song number three on their list of the 10 greatest Adele songs.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

### Europe and Oceania

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Europe and Oceania")\]

Three days after its release, the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company") announced that "Hello" had accumulated 165,000 chart sales in the United Kingdom, of which 156,000 were downloads.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) "Hello" entered at the top of the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on 30 October 2015, – for the week dated 5 November 2015 – with 333,000 combined sales, of which 259,000 were downloads, making it the biggest selling number-one single on the chart in three years. It marked Adele's second UK number-one single, after 2011's "Someone like You". Additionally, "Hello" was streamed 7\.32 million times in its first week, breaking the streaming record previously held by [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[What Do You Mean?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Do_You_Mean%3F "What Do You Mean?")". Including streaming sales and excluding *[The X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")* and *[Pop Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Idol "Pop Idol")* winners' singles, major charity campaign records and Christmas number ones, "Hello" was the second biggest selling number one of the 21st century in the UK, beaten only by [Shaggy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaggy_\(musician\) "Shaggy (musician)")'s "[It Wasn't Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Wasn't_Me "It Wasn't Me")", which sold 345,000 copies in a week in February 2001\.[\[38\]](#cite_note-UK_number_1-38) The following week, the song remained at number one after selling a further 121,000 downloads and was streamed 5\.78 million times, the same week the song was certified Gold by the BPI.[\[39\]](#cite_note-auto-39) On 20 May 2016, it spent its 30th week in the UK Top 100\. As of November 2016, the song has sold 918,700 in pure sales.[\[40\]](#cite_note-UK_sales-40)

The song also debuted at number one in Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Lebanon, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Scotland, Slovakia, Spain and Switzerland.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Idolator-41)

In Australia, "Hello" entered at the top of the [ARIA Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") on 31 October 2015, selling over 59,075 units, which earned the song a gold certification in its first week. The song also became the second fastest-selling single of the year, behind [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa")'s "[See You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/See_You_Again "See You Again")".[\[42\]](#cite_note-maricrisfaderugao-42) It marked Adele's second number-one single on the ARIA Singles Chart following 2011's "Someone like You".[\[43\]](#cite_note-AUS_number_1-43) The single stayed atop the chart for a second week and was certified platinum selling over 70,000 units.[\[42\]](#cite_note-maricrisfaderugao-42) On 20 March 2017, Hello re-entered the chart at number 50 and has so far been certified 7× platinum for sales over 490,000 units.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) In New Zealand, the song debuted at number one on the New Zealand singles chart, holding the position the following week and was certified platinum.[\[41\]](#cite_note-Idolator-41)

### North America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Hello_\(Adele_song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: North America")\]

In the United States, "Hello" debuted at the top of the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on 2 November 2015, for the chart dated 14 November 2015, becoming only the 24th song to debut at number one. "Hello" started at number 49 on the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, after three days of release. In its first full week of airplay, it rose from 45 to 9, up 146% to 70 million all format audience impressions. The track started at number one on the On-Demand Songs chart with a record 20\.4 million on-demand streams, becoming her first number-one song on the chart. "Hello" entered at the top of the [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart with sales of 1,112,000, becoming the first track to sell over one million digital copies in a single week and almost doubling the record for the most downloads sold in a week, previously held by [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida")'s "[Right Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_Round "Right Round")", which sold 636,000 downloads in the week ending 28 February 2009\. "Hello" started with 61\.6 million US streams, becoming her first number-one song and the second greatest weekly total on the [Streaming Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_Songs "Streaming Songs") chart, behind [Baauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baauer "Baauer")'s "[Harlem Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Shake_\(song\) "Harlem Shake (song)")", which registered 103 million streams on week of 3 March 2013\.[\[45\]](#cite_note-US_number_1-45) "Hello" is the first song to sell more than a million digital copies in a single week and the third highest weekly sales total since [Nielsen SoundScan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_SoundScan "Nielsen SoundScan") began tracking sales in 1991\. Only [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John")'s "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")/Something About the Way You Look Tonight" has sold more in a single week, selling 3\.446 million copies in its opening week and 1\.212 million copies in its second week.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

In its second week, "Hello" stayed at number one on the US *Billboard* Hot 100, selling another 635,000 digital copies marking the third-best digital sales week and the highest for a non-debut week. "Hello" also held atop Streaming Songs with 47\.4 million US streams, down 23 percent from 61\.6 million in its first week, the track also stayed atop the On-Demand Songs with 18\.1 million streams. On the Radio Songs chart, "Hello" moved from 9 to 6, up by 46% to 106 million all-format audience impressions, thus becoming the top Airplay Gainer on the Hot 100\. The track also moved from two to one on the Adult Alternative Songs airplay chart and moved nine to four on the Adult Contemporary format.[\[47\]](#cite_note-auto1-47) The following week, the song stayed at the top of the Hot 100 and Digital Songs chart, selling 480,000 downloads and becoming just the third song to sell over 400,000 copies for three straight weeks. "Hello" also rose from 6 to 1 on the Radio Songs chart in just its fourth week (the greatest leap to number one on the chart's 25-year history), marking the quickest climb to number one on the chart in 22 years, since [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")'s "[Dreamlover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamlover_\(Mariah_Carey_song\) "Dreamlover (Mariah Carey song)")" reached the top in its fourth frame on 28 August 1993\. Additionally, "Hello" became just the third song to top the [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100"), Digital Songs, Streaming Songs, On-Demand Songs and Radio Songs tallies simultaneously in the nearly three years all five charts had coexisted.[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) "Hello" remained atop the Hot 100 for ten consecutive weeks, becoming only the 31st No. 1 in the Hot 100's history to reign for at least 10 weeks, and only the 4th for a number one debut, following "[One Sweet Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Sweet_Day "One Sweet Day")" by Mariah Carey and [Boyz II Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyz_II_Men "Boyz II Men") (16 weeks), "Candle in the Wind 1997/Something About the Way You Look Tonight" by Elton John (14 weeks) and [I'll Be Missing You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Be_Missing_You "I'll Be Missing You") by [Puff Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Combs "Sean Combs") & [Faith Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Evans "Faith Evans") featuring [112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/112_\(band\) "112 (band)") (11 weeks). By spending a tenth week at the top of the chart, it became Adele's longest-running number-one single and the longest-leading Hot 100 No. 1 by a solo female since [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna")'s "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")," featuring [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris"), which also led for 10 weeks in 2011–2012. The accompanying music video for "Hello" was directed by Canadian actor and filmmaker [Xavier Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Dolan "Xavier Dolan") and released on 23 October 2015, despite the fact the song was released as a single a day later.[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) The concept of the video revolves around a recently broken-up young woman calling a younger version of herself.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89) Portions of the video—mostly the finale on the pond and the shot of her opening her eyes in the beginning—were filmed with [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") cameras, making it the first music video in IMAX format.[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) The video draws inspiration from Dolan's semi-autobiographical debut *[I Killed My Mother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Killed_My_Mother "I Killed My Mother")*, which was made when Dolan was barely 20\.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89) The video was filmed on a farm in [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") over four days in September 2015\.[\[89\]](#cite_note-LATimes-89)

The video stars American actor [Tristan Wilds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tristan_Wilds "Tristan Wilds"). **Barcode analysis** (per-column average colors):
- **Overall palette**: light, heavily desaturated warm grays, sepia tans, rosy beiges (`#b19e98`, `#c6af98`, `#cac1c1`) with occasional pale olive-greens (`#a3cb93`, `#b8beab`) and pale blues — a classic muted "film grade" look. No saturated colors anywhere except two salmon/red stripes at the very start.
- **Structure**: ~170 stripes ≈ 2.2s each → a ~6-minute video. Opens with reddish/sepia stripes (an extreme warm-toned face close-up), moves to greens (forest), then long muted interior/outdoor tones, then blue-gray stripes at ~92%, and ends in a long near-white section (bright snowy finale).

**Candidate comparison**:
- The kids' videos (CoComelon, Miroshka TV, LooLoo Kids), "Shake It Off", "Sorry", and "Something Just Like This" are all highly saturated — ruled out.
- "See You Again" and "Counting Stars" thumbnails are much darker (garage/basement scenes, night footage) — their barcodes would be far darker than this light barcode.

**"Hello" (Adele) matches every feature**: Wikipedia confirms the video is **sepia toned**, shot in a small house and a **wooded forest** (the green stripes), with the **finale on a frozen pond** (the blue-gray stripes at 92–94% followed by a washed-out bright white ending as the sun breaks through), and opens with the famous warm, sunlit IMAX close-up of her opening her eyes (the reddish-salmon first stripes). The video length (~6:07) matches the stripe count at "a few seconds" per stripe.
